DIMS.name: Enterprise Profile
DIMS.summary: Airline Demo is a complex global passenger airline with cargo, loyalty, maintenance, and digital operations.

DIMS.name: Business Functions
DIMS.summary: Flight operations, crew management, customer experience, maintenance, and sourcing are the primary AI-relevant functions.

DIMS.name: Org Ownership
DIMS.summary: Policy content ownership and data governance accountability are not yet assigned across critical use cases.

DIMS.name: Workforce Roles
DIMS.summary: Crew planners, contact center agents, maintenance technicians, and sourcing analysts are primary AI-adjacent roles.

DIMS.name: Applications & Systems
DIMS.summary: Fourteen systems span reservations, crew, maintenance, baggage, CRM, loyalty, ITSM, and data platforms.

DIMS.name: Data Assets & Integrations
DIMS.summary: Key data domains including disruption lineage, bag scans, maintenance events, and transcripts lack certification.

DIMS.name: Infrastructure & Platforms
DIMS.summary: AWS airline data lakehouse is a target-state platform; current-state certification evidence is not yet confirmed.

DIMS.name: Vendors & Contracts
DIMS.summary: Eight vendors including NorthSky Managed Services and AeroCore anchor critical operational and IT delivery.

DIMS.name: IT Budget, Spend & Value
DIMS.summary: Flight operations, crew management, customer experience, maintenance, and sourcing are the primary AI-relevant functions.

DIMS.name: Programs & Initiatives
DIMS.summary: Seven active use-case programs span sourcing, operations, customer experience, and analytics modernization.

DIMS.name: AI & Automation Use Cases
DIMS.summary: Airline Demo is a complex global passenger airline with cargo, loyalty, maintenance, and digital operations.

DIMS.name: Risks & Controls
DIMS.summary: Risk spans managed-services contract gaps, uncertified data lineage, and unvalidated AI governance controls.

DIMS.name: Relationships
DIMS.summary: CIO, CTO, and CDAO teams share overlapping priorities but cross-functional alignment is not yet evidenced.

DIMS.name: Evidence Sources
DIMS.summary: Current evidence is planning-grade and synthetic; no production-certified data, contracts, or outcomes are claimed.

DIMS.name: Metrics & Outcomes
DIMS.summary: No certified operational, financial, or customer-experience baselines exist to anchor outcome measurement.

DIMS.name: Industry Context Patterns
DIMS.summary: IROPS sensitivity, crew legality complexity, and managed-services dependency are common airline transformation risks.

DIMS.name: Expert Lenses
DIMS.summary: Legal, procurement, data governance, AI ethics, and operational safety expertise are required across use cases.

DIMS.name: Managed Services Scope
DIMS.summary: NorthSky Managed Services anchors AMS and IMS delivery; scope, SLAs, and exit terms are not yet validated.

DIMS.name: Operational Process Evidence
DIMS.summary: Risk spans managed-services contract gaps, uncertified data lineage, and unvalidated AI governance controls.

profile.meaning: Airline Demo is a complex global passenger airline with cargo, loyalty, maintenance, and digital operations.
profile.observed: Seven strategic use cases span sourcing, IROPS, crew, contact center, maintenance, and baggage domains.
profile.matters: Operational reliability and managed-services dependency create compounding risk across fragmented evidence layers.
profile.supports: No use case is decision-grade until cross-domain evidence is reconciled and governance owners are confirmed.

functions.meaning: Flight operations, crew management, customer experience, maintenance, and sourcing are the primary AI-relevant functions.
functions.observed: IROPS, crew recovery, contact center, and baggage functions share overlapping data and system dependencies.
functions.matters: Function-level fragmentation means AI use cases cannot be sequenced without cross-function data governance.
functions.supports: Function readiness is hypothesis-grade; no function has certified end-to-end data lineage confirmed.

org.meaning: Policy content ownership and data governance accountability are not yet assigned across critical use cases.
org.observed: Contact center policy ownership, crew rule lineage, and maintenance safety controls lack confirmed accountable owners.
org.matters: Without named owners, AI outputs cannot be approved, audited, or operationally trusted by frontline teams.
org.supports: Ownership gaps are a governance blocker; no AI use case should advance to production without resolution.

workforce.meaning: Crew planners, contact center agents, maintenance technicians, and sourcing analysts are primary AI-adjacent roles.
workforce.observed: Agent assist, crew recovery, and maintenance analytics each require role-specific acceptance and QA telemetry.
workforce.matters: Without operator acceptance evidence, AI recommendations risk rejection or unsafe override in operational settings.
workforce.supports: Role readiness is not yet evidenced; human override capture and QA telemetry are prerequisites for deployment.

apps.meaning: Fourteen systems span reservations, crew, maintenance, baggage, CRM, loyalty, ITSM, and data platforms.
apps.observed: Legacy reservations and enterprise data warehouse coexist with target-state AWS lakehouse and modern ITSM.
apps.matters: System fragmentation creates integration risk that blocks real-time AI use cases across IROPS and contact center.
apps.supports: Application dependency mapping is planning-grade; real-time integration evidence is missing for critical use cases.

data.meaning: Key data domains including disruption lineage, bag scans, maintenance events, and transcripts lack certification.
data.observed: Cross-system data lineage is unproven for IROPS, baggage, maintenance, and contact center use cases.
data.matters: Uncertified data foundations make AI outputs unreliable and expose the enterprise to operational and regulatory risk.
data.supports: All data-dependent use cases are hypothesis-grade until lineage, completeness, and quality are formally validated.

infra.meaning: AWS airline data lakehouse is a target-state platform; current-state certification evidence is not yet confirmed.
infra.observed: Legacy enterprise data warehouse remains the operational anchor while lakehouse migration is in progress.
infra.matters: Uncertified target infrastructure blocks analytics modernization and AI use cases dependent on lakehouse feeds.
infra.supports: Infrastructure readiness is planning-grade; no AI use case should assume lakehouse availability without certification.

vendors.meaning: Eight vendors including NorthSky Managed Services and AeroCore anchor critical operational and IT delivery.
vendors.observed: Managed-services dependency is high; SLA commitments, exit rights, and benchmarking terms are not validated.
vendors.matters: Unvalidated vendor controls create sourcing leverage risk and limit renegotiation options without legal review.
vendors.supports: Vendor dependency is a sourcing risk; no renegotiation or exit strategy should proceed without contract evidence.

budget.meaning: Flight operations, crew management, customer experience, maintenance, and sourcing are the primary AI-relevant functions.
budget.observed: IROPS, crew recovery, contact center, and baggage functions share overlapping data and system dependencies.
budget.matters: Function-level fragmentation means AI use cases cannot be sequenced without cross-function data governance.
budget.supports: Function readiness is hypothesis-grade; no function has certified end-to-end data lineage confirmed.

programs.meaning: Seven active use-case programs span sourcing, operations, customer experience, and analytics modernization.
programs.observed: Program interdependencies are high; IROPS, crew, and contact center programs share unresolved data dependencies.
programs.matters: Sequencing errors across interdependent programs risk compounding delays and misallocated transformation investment.
programs.supports: Program sequencing is a hypothesis; no program should advance to execution without dependency mapping evidence.

ai.meaning: Airline Demo is a complex global passenger airline with cargo, loyalty, maintenance, and digital operations.
ai.observed: Seven strategic use cases span sourcing, IROPS, crew, contact center, maintenance, and baggage domains.
ai.matters: Operational reliability and managed-services dependency create compounding risk across fragmented evidence layers.
ai.supports: No use case is decision-grade until cross-domain evidence is reconciled and governance owners are confirmed.

risks.meaning: Risk spans managed-services contract gaps, uncertified data lineage, and unvalidated AI governance controls.
risks.observed: SLA misses without business-impact linkage, unreconciled service credits, and missing safety controls are key risks.
risks.matters: Unmitigated risks in vendor contracts and AI data foundations can escalate to operational and regulatory consequences.
risks.supports: Risk posture is not yet evidenced as controlled; each risk domain requires owner assignment and mitigation evidence.

rel.meaning: CIO, CTO, and CDAO teams share overlapping priorities but cross-functional alignment is not yet evidenced.
rel.observed: Interview signals show consistent pain points across technology, infrastructure, and data leadership teams.
rel.matters: Misaligned stakeholder priorities create sequencing conflicts and slow evidence collection across use cases.
rel.supports: Stakeholder alignment is a hypothesis; formal cross-functional governance is needed before program commitments.

evidence.meaning: Current evidence is planning-grade and synthetic; no production-certified data, contracts, or outcomes are claimed.
evidence.observed: Interview signals, use-case gap lists, and system inventories form the current evidence base for all analysis.
evidence.matters: Synthetic evidence supports framing and hypothesis generation but cannot support production or sourcing decisions.
evidence.supports: All analysis is advisory until real contracts, invoices, SLA reports, and certified data feeds are validated.

metrics.meaning: No certified operational, financial, or customer-experience baselines exist to anchor outcome measurement.
metrics.observed: IROPS recovery time, agent handle time, crew recovery cost, and baggage claim rates lack approved baselines.
metrics.matters: Without baselines, AI transformation value cannot be measured, reported, or defended to executive stakeholders.
metrics.supports: Outcome claims are hypothesis-grade; value measurement requires approved baselines before any AI deployment.

industry.meaning: IROPS sensitivity, crew legality complexity, and managed-services dependency are common airline transformation risks.
industry.observed: Industry patterns suggest data lineage gaps and vendor lock-in are systemic challenges in airline AI programs.
industry.matters: Industry context validates that Airline Demo's gaps are not unique but require airline-specific mitigation approaches.
industry.supports: Industry benchmarks are directional only; Airline Demo-specific evidence must validate any pattern-based hypothesis.

lenses.meaning: Legal, procurement, data governance, AI ethics, and operational safety expertise are required across use cases.
lenses.observed: No single expert lens covers the full scope; cross-domain expert engagement is a prerequisite for evidence validation.
lenses.matters: Missing expert review in legal, safety, and AI governance domains creates unmitigated risk in transformation planning.
lenses.supports: Expert engagement is a planning prerequisite; no use case should advance without domain-specific expert sign-off.

ms.meaning: NorthSky Managed Services anchors AMS and IMS delivery; scope, SLAs, and exit terms are not yet validated.
ms.observed: SLA commitments are not mapped to business criticality; change-order leakage and rate-card variance are hypothesized.
ms.matters: Unvalidated managed-services scope limits sourcing leverage and blocks defensible renegotiation or exit planning.
